issue.title: Scheduler stop kills in-process chop launch batch with no drain or resume
issue.description:
## Bug

- **Location:** `src/sase/axe/chop_runner.py` routine SIGTERM handler (`_running = False`) + service-host ~10s SIGKILL of the scheduler process group; unlaunched proposals in `launch_chop_proposals` (`src/sase/axe/chop_proposal_launch.py` / `multi_prompt_launch_execution.py` loop) are neither persisted nor resumed

A scheduler or service-host stop gives a chop's in-process proposal launch loop no chance to drain. The routine's SIGTERM handler only sets `_running = False`, and the host SIGKILLs after about 10 s. Unlaunched proposals are neither persisted nor resumed, so a clan ends up partially launched and then blocks its own chop.

Evidence: athena 2026-09-28 `toobig_split[sase]` chop run `20260928T093200_850344` (routine `run_every`) started launching 61-member clan `toobig-68`; members 1-2 created 09:32:28/09:32:37; user `Q` -> `3/a` at 09:32:53 re-exec'd TUI, new TUI ran `systemctl --user restart sase.service` 09:33:00, old host SIGKILL-stopped by 09:33:11 killing routine mid-launch-loop; 59 launches lost silently. Half-launched clan blocked chop ("inhibited by active agent clan `toobig-68`") until leftovers killed 09:33:42/09:58:17; 09:58:25 run launched complete `toobig-69`. Verified afterwards: no `toobig-68` procs left, both members DONE (dismissed), no workspace/project-file claims, `toobig-69` launching normally. Do not touch athena.

Candidate directions:
- drain or extend the stop grace while a launch batch is active;
- persist remaining proposals for resume;
- add the same guard to `sase scheduler stop`, `sase service restart` and the Services-tab stop/restart actions.
